name: page
description: The graph page: the ruled paper everything on a screen is written on. Full width at 390; from 700 an object of its own, exactly 40 graph modules wide (--page-w) and centred, running the full height; at 1200 it starts at the title block's edge. A split page lays its content in two columns at desktop.

layout.description: split (was .page.split): from 1200, a grid of the record and a 340px second column (Timeline's index, the answer's sources), every item start-aligned (revision 39 and after).

head.description: What heads the page, which sets its lead at 1200 (was .page.pushed, .page.pushed.untitled, .page.bare): title, the masthead row; pushed, the back control and the title; untitled, the back control alone; bare, nothing.

scrolled.description: iOS only: the screen scrolled, its large title gone (was .page.scrolled). The record moves up by --aj-l-page-overflow, which whoever shows the state sets (the mobile-app comp measures 292px).

reader.description: A walkthrough's navbar page (the prototypes and the website, mobile and tablet): the reader's label, "<reader> content". Given, the page puts its children in the scrolling reader (data-place reader) between the header and the foot; empty, it writes header, children and foot in order.

accepts: the screen's content: masthead (row form), destinations, sheets, components
children.description: The page's blocks, in reading order (with header and foot: what goes between them).

accepts: the header section (static or navbar form)

foot.description: Last, after the reader when there is one.

places.block: an object in the page column: the page gutter, --s6 below
places.record: the day's record (the sheet): more space below it at desktop; on iOS it never shrinks
places.foot: the composer: pushed to the foot of the page
places.main: the single-purpose object (the stack): grows; capped at 700 and centred at desktop
places.aside: the split page's second column (the calendar, the panel)
places.column: with aside: the aside runs the whole height of the record's column on a split page (the Timeline's sticky date and mood card, v4 C1)
places.grow: takes the room left (the auth spread)
places.head: the masthead row: pinned to the top below desktop while the page scrolls under it
places.reader: the scrolling reader on a navbar page (mobile and tablet walkthroughs), rendered by the page (option reader): it holds the page's blocks between the pinned header and the composer; the page then fills the view and does not scroll
places.fill: with block: an object that is the page's whole view (Ask's chat): the page gutter, nothing below it, so its sticky foot rests on the view's bottom edge

exposes.--aj-l-page-lead: The space above a single page's first object at desktop, by its head (data-head); the split page starts its columns there too.
exposes.--aj-l-page-overflow: How far a scrolled iOS page has moved (scrolled): set by whoever shows the state; the mobile-app comp sets 292px in lock.css.
exposes.--aj-l-page-lead-set: An override of the lead the website's runtime sets on its navbar page (0): it drops the lead.
exposes.--aj-l-page-view-height: The height of a navbar page: the view less the browser's own furniture, set by the app (the website runtime) as it lays the page out.

states.loading: n/a: a surface; loading belongs to what it holds
states.error: n/a: a surface; errors belong to what it holds
states.empty: n/a: a page always holds content; an empty journal is the empty state component

a11y.role: none of its own: a generic container. The landmarks (header, nav, main) are its children

responsive.700: width 100% capped at --page-w, centred, min-height 1120px (revision 19); the gutter doubles to --s8 (set by legacy CSS on .page until its readers migrate)
responsive.1200: min-height 784px; starts at --title-w with no right margin; split lays out two columns

changelog.change: Converted from lock.css A2 (.page) and the website preview's page rules.
Option scrolled (data-scrolled), was the legacy class .scrolled; --aj-l-page-overflow is set directly, the legacy --overflow is gone.
Option reader and slots header, view and foot: the walkthrough's navbar page is rendered by the page modules (pages round 5), not rewritten at build (scripts/web-headers.mjs addReader, retired).
The sidebar page's margins and the pinned head below desktop key on the container's 1200, no longer on the stage's platform (v4 D1); same weight, no visual change.
Place column (with aside): on a split page the aside spans every row of the record's column, so the Timeline's date and mood card can stick beside the whole list (v4 C1).
The view slot and place: they held the timeline's List/Calendar zoom, gone in v4 C1. The split's comment now says what the split is (Timeline's card, Ask's sources), not the calendar index's history.
